data.title: Strong rupee keeps India rice rates anchored near 19-month peak
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indian rice export prices hit highest since March 2025
  • Thai prices rise to highest level since October 2024
  • Vietnam's domestic supplies of broken rice running low-traders
  • Bangladesh lowers rice import forecast on higher domestic supplies

By Vishak Mathew

Indian rice export prices climbed to a more than 19-month high this week on a stronger rupee and robust overseas demand, while Thai rates touched a more than two-year peak on steady demand from Japan and the Philippines amid fears of a dip in output.

The rupee's appreciation is prompting exporters to raise prices to protect their margins, said a Mumbai-based dealer with a trade house.

India's 5% broken parboiled variety (RI-INBKN5-P1) was quoted at $396-$401 per ton this week, up from last week's $394-$398. Indian 5% broken white rice was priced at $398-$403 per ton.

India is considering imposing export duties on certain rice varieties to improve its domestic supplies and mitigate price increases that consumers and industries face in its home market.

Vietnam's 5% broken rice (RI-VNBKN5-P1) was offered at $475-$485 per metric ton on Thursday, unchanged from a week ago.

"India's plans to impose export duties on certain rice varieties to improve its domestic supplies haven't had any impact on export prices of Vietnamese rice," a trader based in Ho Chi Minh City said.

"We are closely monitoring India's next moves," the trader said.

Traders said Vietnam's domestic supplies of broken rice are running low.

Thailand's 5% broken rice (RI-THBKN5-P1) rose to $520 per ton this week before easing to $510, the highest level since October 17, 2024, compared to the range of $505 to $510 per ton last week.

Higher prices were driven by exporters buying to cover short positions, a trader said.

There have been vessels arriving to load cargoes, with purchases from the Philippines as well as regular customers in Japan, the trader added.

The harvest of the main-season fragrant rice crop in the Northeast has begun and the trader expects output to decline due to flooding.

Elsewhere, Bangladesh's rice import forecast for trade year 2026-27 has been lowered by 0.4 million metric tons to 1.1 million tons, from 1.5 million tons, as higher domestic supplies reduce the need for foreign purchases, according to the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA).

However, domestic rice prices remained high despite ample supplies.

data.title: Swara Baby Products fixes price band for ₹800 crore IPO - Details here
data.description:
Swara Baby Products Ltd., a baby hygiene and personal care manufacturer known for baby diapers, wipes and infant care essentials, has fixed the price band for its ₹800 crore Initial Public Offering (IPO) on Friday, November 27.

The company plans to sell shares in a price band of ₹105 to ₹111 per share, with eligible employees getting a discount of ₹10 per share on the issue price. Each share carries a face value of ₹2 each. Shares will be listed both on the BSE and the NSE.

The ₹800 crore IPO will comprise of a fresh issue of shares worth ₹498.75 crore, and the rest being an Offer For Sale (OFS) component.

One lot of the Swara Baby Products IPO will comprise of 135 shares. Retail investors will have to make a minimum investment of ₹14,985, to apply for one lot of shares. 35% of the total IPO has been reserved for retail investors.

50% of the issue is reserved for Qualified Institutional Bidders (QIBs), while the rest is reserved for non-institutional investors.

At the upper end of the price band, Swara Baby Products Limited commands a pre-issue market capitalization of ₹2,711.56 crore, which will rise to ₹3,210.31 crore post-issue. Promoter shareholding currently stands at 100.00% and will dilute to 75.12% upon completion of the offering. JM Financial and Avendus Capital are acting as the Book Running Lead Managers (BRLMs) to the issue, while MUFG Intime India Private Limited has been appointed as the registrar.

According to the indicative schedule, the basis of allotment will be finalized on December 7, 2026. Both the initiation of refunds (or unblocking of ASBA funds) and the credit of equity shares to successful applicants' demat accounts are expected to take place on December 8, 2026, ahead of the tentative stock market debut on December 9, 2026.

data.title: StarHub-M1 Merger Likely Faces Limited Opposition From Singapore Regulators — Market Talk
data.description: StarHub's merger with telecommunications peer M1 should face only limited opposition from Singapore regulators, says BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions, in a note. The regulators likely recognize that having four telecommunications operators in Singapore to serve a saturated market harms investment rather than protects consumer choice, BMI says. The merger would bring the number of operators in the city-state to three. However, the StarHub-M1 combination would also leave the smallest operator, Simba Telecom, in a very weak position and risk the number of players in the market shrinking to two. BMI reckons the regulators could call for the combined StarHub-M1 entity to transfer some assets to Simba to ensure a degree of competitiveness. (megan.cheah@wsj.com)

data.title: Chinese industrial profit rises 16% in January-October
data.description:
Profit at Chinese industrial firms rose 16% in the first 10 months of this year over the corresponding period last year, official data showed on Friday.

The increase quickened from 15.5% in the January-September period, showed data from the National Bureau of Statistics.

Industrial profit figures cover firms with annual revenue of at least 20 million yuan ($3 million) from main operations.

data.title: Vysarn Targeting 34% FY27 Profit Growth on Welltech Acquisition and Water Services Recovery
data.description:
Vysarn Limited is targeting net profit before tax (NPBT) of $28 million for the 2027 financial year, supported by the acquisition of Welltech and an anticipated increase in activity across its established water services businesses.

The Perth-based group outlined its growth ambitions at its annual general meeting on 26 November, targeting a 34% increase in NPBT and growth of approximately 20% in fully diluted EPS.

The outlook follows a record FY26 result, when operational revenue climbed 31% to $140.1m and NPBT rose 39% to $20.9m.

Vysarn expects earnings to be weighted heavily towards the second half of FY27 as project delivery accelerates, drilling fleet utilisation increases, and Welltech contributes a full six months of earnings.

Broader National Footprint

Vysarn completed its acquisition of Welltech in September for upfront consideration of $50m, with up to a further $10m payable over three years depending on earnings hurdles.

The transaction followed a fully underwritten $65.3m placement at $1.05 per share, with proceeds allocated to the acquisition, development of the Kariyarra Water Scheme (KWS), growth initiatives, transaction costs, and working capital.

Welltech has performed in line with expectations since completion, and Vysarn has brought forward plans for its east coast expansion after winning a master service agreement with Melbourne Water to provide sewerage bypass services.

The business will establish premises in Victoria in the second half, drawing on the wider group’s customer relationships to pursue additional work across the utilities, civil construction and resources sectors.

Drilling Fleet Supports Growth

Vysarn’s Industrial division generated NPBT of $11.5m in FY26 and has reshaped its drilling fleet through acquisitions and rebuilds to broaden its specialist capabilities.

The group expects to have 12 rigs operating during the second half of FY27, with a 13th available to cover scheduled maintenance or additional demand and opportunities to operate up to three rigs on double shifts.

A five-year contract with a major iron ore customer supports the deployment of multiple rigs, while existing contracts and indicative demand underpin the anticipated increase in drilling activity.

Vysarn’s Advisory division is targeting earnings growth through the conversion of its first-half tender pipeline, while its Technology business expects wastewater treatment plant projects and managed aquifer recharge work to support FY27 performance.

Water Scheme Approvals

The KWS joint venture has submitted its final technical assessment supporting an application to extract up to 10 gigalitres of groundwater annually, with the proposed development now based on a 15-year project life.

Vysarn’s board now anticipates receiving an undertaking for a groundwater licence from the Department of Water and Environmental Regulation in the second half of FY27, while environmental and land tenure approvals remain outstanding.

Expenditure on the KWS totalled $8.9m at 31 October, with up to $10m of additional funding allocated from the July capital raising subject to requirements.

Negotiations with Water Corporation over a bulk water supply agreement for Port Hedland have progressed, with non-binding expressions of interest from the broader market exceeding the volume sought under the licence application.

Vysarn is targeting binding offtake or option agreements during FY27 alongside in-principle infrastructure funding as it works towards the regulatory approvals required to develop the scheme.

data.title: Japan, South Korea indices rise: Asian markets extend gains as AI stocks rebound
data.description:
Asian equities extended their rebound on Friday, November 27, as investors returned to artificial intelligence (AI) stocks after weeks of choppy trading.

The MSCI Asia Pacific index gained 0.6%, its second straight daily advance, with benchmarks in Japan moved higher, and South Korea opened higher before paring some of its gains.

In Tokyo, the Topix added 0.85% and the Nikkei 225 inched up 0.010%, while South Korea's Kospi gained 0.67%. Hang Seng futures fell 0.4%. Taiwan's TAIEX however, slipped 0.15% at open.

In Japan, Tokyo's consumer price index, excluding fresh food, rose 2.9% in November from a year earlier, the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications reported, the highest reading since July 2025. The measure which the Bank of Japan closely watches to understand underlying inflation, climbed 2.5%, while headline CPI rose 2.8%.

Tokyo's inflation number is significant since it often foreshadows national trends, indicating possibilities for a rate hike by the Japan's central bank next month.

Wall Street looked set to follow as futures on the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 each rose 0.7% ahead of a shortened US session after the Thanksgiving holiday. European shares also closed higher on Thursday, and that upbeat tone pushed copper up almost 2% from an 11-month low in London.

In India, the GIFT Nifty hinted towards a muted start in the red for the country's indices. Attention for the day's trade was particularly centered on the Nifty, which needed to close above 25,800 to secure a fifth successive weekly gain. The index last managed such a streak in June and July 2024, when it rose for eight weeks running.

US tariff plans add to the unease in the country after Washington proposed 25% duties on Indian imports on Wednesday, with a cap of 17% if the two countries agree a bilateral trade deal. According to experts cited by PTI, India's exporters could be at a disadvantage because the Section 301 excess-capacity probe covers only 14 trading partners and excludes rivals such as Pakistan, Sri Lanka, the Philippines and Turkiye.

In currency markets, the Japaneseyen held near 159.31 per dollar and the offshore yuan stayed close to 6.6610.

US Treasuries, meanwhile, fell as cash trading resumed, lifting the yield on the benchmark 10-year note two basis points to 4.87%.

Traders, however, seem to doubt the rally will last. Thursday's tech-led gains across Asia and Europe followed days of volatility driven by questions over the AI trade, and few catalysts appear ready to sustain the recovery. Investors now are likely to look to next month's US Federal Reserve meeting for hints on where borrowing costs are heading.

Oil prices meanwhile rose after Yemen's Houthi rebels attacked a major Saudi refinery. Brent crude climbed more than 2% to above $96 a barrel for January delivery, extending gains of over 6% across the previous two sessions, while West Texas Intermediate gained 1.5% to trade near $85.

Saudi Arabia's press agency, citing an unnamed Energy Ministry source, said the Iran-backed group struck the Jazan refinery on the Red Sea coast, halting some operations, killing one worker and injuring several others. The 400,000-barrel-a-day plant is the latest target in a run of regional attacks. The Houthis also claimed a strike on the 500,000-barrel-a-day Ras Tanura refinery, which Riyadh has not confirmed.

With Agency Inputs

data.title: AECOM to manage $15bn Adani infrastructure programmes in India
data.description:
Infrastructure consultancy AECOM has been hired to provide programme management for three multi-year Adani Group infrastructure schemes in India with a combined capital value of about $15bn, the company announced on November 23.

The appointment covers renewable power generation, electricity transmission and airport expansion. These sectors are central to the Indian government's Viksit Bharat plan to make the country a leading global economy by 2047. AECOM said the work would also help grow India's clean energy market and build up the infrastructure needed for long-term growth.

AECOM's role as Program Management Consultant covers the biggest of the three, the Khavda Renewable Energy Plant, a 30-gigawatt facility in Gujarat in western India that pairs battery energy storage systems with wind and solar power. The company said the programme ranks among the world's largest in renewable energy.

A second programme is set to deliver four transmission and substation projects spanning Gujarat and Maharashtra. These are intended to form a green energy corridor linking large renewable generation hubs with centres of high demand such as Mumbai. They are also meant to improve grid resilience and allow the network to absorb more renewable power.

The third assignment involves overseeing management, coordination and delivery across Adani's airport expansion in Ahmedabad, Mangaluru and Thiruvananthapuram. That programme aims to raise passenger capacity and improve regional connectivity.

'AECOM brings deep global expertise in program management across the energy and aviation sectors, underpinned by a strong local presence in India,' said Richard Whitehead, chief executive of AECOM's Europe & India region.

'We're proud to support Adani Group in delivering these ambitious energy and aviation infrastructure programs,' said Suvojoy Sengupta, chief executive of AECOM's business in India. 'Clean energy and improved connectivity will be critical to achieving India's Viksit Bharat vision, and we look forward to working closely with our client to help bring these transformative projects to life.'
